negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned no HU LinkedIn aggregator or open API mirror; LinkedIn itself is auth-walled and ToS-restricted.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A significant fraction of HU payments weak signals (role changes, project go-lives, partnership posts) appear first on LinkedIn and will be missed by web-only collection.

negative_findings.description: No speaker list or detailed agenda could be obtained for the Budapest TechShow X (merged PayTechShow/BankTechShow) edition from the aggregator page found; the aggregator described tracks but did not name speakers.
negative_findings.result_summary: Track topics described (cards, instant payments/AFR, POS, softPOS, acquiring, ISO 20022, IPR) but no named speakers; organiser's own domain not confirmed in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The speaker list is the actual intelligence asset (who is building what); without it the event is only a calendar entry.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian equivalent of a structured startup-funding database (Crunchbase-style, HU-specific, open) was found for payment/fintech rounds. Funding signals are scattered across trade press (FinTechZone), general media (Infostart, Piac&Profit) and investor sites.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only narrative media coverage and investor-side pages; no structured HU funding dataset located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Funding-round tracking will require entity extraction from prose rather than a clean feed, raising cost and error rate.

negative_findings.description: Profession.hu and hu.indeed.com were observed only through search-result summaries in this pass; their robots.txt, rate limits and anti-bot posture were not tested. Job boards commonly return 403 to automated clients.
negative_findings.result_summary: No fetch attempted/confirmed; access status recorded as unverified rather than blocked.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Hiring signal is a core part of this cell; if these boards block automation the workstream needs a manual or licensed-feed fallback.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Hungarian and English for a data.gov.hu-style national open-data portal hosting machine-readable payment/card/ATM datasets. The Hungarian landscape is a public-data cadastre and metadata search (kozadatportal.hu, opendata.gov.hu, kozadat.hu) rather than a CKAN dataset store, and no payment/card dataset was actually observed in them during this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Portals identified as pointers, but no concrete HU payment dataset record confirmed inside them.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents over-promising open-data coverage; the operational archive for HU payment series remains MNB's own archive plus web archives.

negative_findings.description: No established Hungarian-language term or portal convention was found for 'discontinued/withdrawn dataset' beyond MNB's own 'archív tartalmak' and KSH's 'archív' labelling; there is no HU equivalent of a formal dataset-deprecation registry.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local vocabulary limited to 'archív tartalmak', 'megszűnt tábla', 'korábbi idősor'.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Query design must lean on those three phrases; broader deprecation vocabulary will not retrieve HU results.

negative_findings.description: The OSZK national web archive, the strongest local complement to the Internet Archive, is largely closed for copyright reasons with only three small public sub-collections.
negative_findings.result_summary: Access requires a research arrangement via webarchivum@oszk.hu.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated recovery of withdrawn HU bank/MNB pages from the national archive is not possible; Wayback remains the only self-serve route.

negative_findings.description: Pre-1990 Hungarian statistical yearbooks are digitised but sit behind the Arcanum ADT subscription; no free full-text route was found in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Subscription/library access required.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Long-run cash/monetary baselines are obtainable only with an institutional subscription or via KSH Library.

negative_findings.description: opendata.hu was described in the sources mainly in past tense and its current liveness was not established. Recorded as unverified, not dead.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hypothesis: possibly dormant; requires a deterministic liveness pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids recording a false negative for a catalogue that may still mirror withdrawn HU datasets.

negative_findings.description: Despite searching in Hungarian for aggregate online cash-register statistics (NAV online pénztárgép összesített adatok, készpénzes/kártyás tranzakció statisztika), no evidence was found that NAV publishes an open aggregate series of cash-register turnover split by payment mode. All located NAV cash-register data services are scoped to the individual taxpayer's own registers.
negative_findings.result_summary: NAV's M2M cash-register download exists but is per-taxpayer; no public payment-mode aggregate located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single richest potential HU cash-vs-card dataset appears to be non-public; obtaining it would require an FOI (közérdekű adatigénylés) or a research agreement, which changes the collection plan fundamentally.

negative_findings.description: No standalone STADAT table dedicated to payment method in retail (kiskereskedelmi forgalom fizetési mód szerint) was found. Payment-method splits appear only inside KSH ICT/e-commerce survey narrative publications, not as a maintained table.
negative_findings.result_summary: Payment-mode data exists in KSH ICT publications but not as a structured, machine-readable STADAT series.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Time-series construction will require PDF extraction rather than table download, and comparability across years must be checked each edition.

negative_findings.description: Searches in Hungarian for a KSH open/JSON API (STADAT API, adatletöltés, nyílt adat) surfaced only the STADAT HTML/XLSX tables and the STATINFO interactive database with a documented ~40,000-cell display limit; no official public REST/JSON statistical API was identified.
negative_findings.result_summary: No confirmed KSH public statistical API found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must assume file-level scraping of XLSX/CSV rather than an API contract, raising maintenance cost and breakage risk.

negative_findings.description: No ÁSZ (State Audit Office) analysis dedicated specifically to cash usage (készpénzhasználat) was located; only adjacent analyses on financial awareness/digitalisation and on tech industry/e-commerce.
negative_findings.result_summary: Adjacent ÁSZ material only; no cash-usage-specific audit analysis found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents over-claiming ÁSZ as a cash-usage source; it remains a low-priority adjacent watch item.

negative_findings.description: Fetched https://www.giro.hu/ and read its navigation (Szolgáltatások, Társaságunk, Dokumentumok, Panaszkezelés, Karrier, Kapcsolat, Rendszer információ). No top-level 'Statisztika' or 'Forgalmi adatok' section exists on the operator's own site.
negative_findings.result_summary: GIRO does not maintain a visible, navigable statistics landing page; volume PDFs surface only as hashed /storage/ assets reachable through the document listing or search engines.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any collection pipeline that assumes a stable statistics URL for GIRO will fail. Collection must be built on the /dokumentumok listing (and its /api/documents/{id} pattern), or fall back to MNB's statisztika portal for BKR series.

negative_findings.description: Repeated Hungarian searches for 'BKR tranzakciók száma' PDFs returned only 2021 and 2022 vintages (covering data to 2021/2022). No 2023–2026 vintage of the BKR forgalmi statisztika was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only stale public vintages of the GIRO-published monthly BKR transaction-count series were found via search.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The headline AFR uptake series may have been discontinued at source, moved behind the document listing, or simply not indexed. This is a hypothesis, not a verdict — a direct crawl of giro.hu/dokumentumok is required before concluding the series is dead.

negative_findings.description: The Hungarian phrase 'forgalmi adatok' is heavily polluted: searches surfaced BKK (Budapest public transport) traffic datasets on opendata.gov.hu and bkk.hu rather than payment clearing turnover.
negative_findings.result_summary: 'forgalmi adatok' alone is unusable as a query term for this cell; it must be paired with BKR/GIRO/elszámolás/tranzakciószám.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Query templates for automated discovery must disambiguate, otherwise the pipeline ingests transport traffic data as payments data.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated GIRO Zrt. press room / sajtószoba or news feed was identified in the site navigation or via search; operator-sourced figures reach the public mainly through MNB press releases and trade press interviews.
negative_findings.result_summary: GIRO has no discoverable owned media channel for statistics announcements.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Monitoring must be routed via MNB sajtóközlemények and fintech trade press rather than an operator RSS feed, which adds latency and a second-hand-attribution risk.

negative_findings.description: No public statistical API or machine-readable open-data endpoint was found for GIRO/BKR volumes; KELER offers CSV downloads but no documented API, and the ECB Data Portal is the only API-grade source touching HU clearing statistics found in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Collection for this cell will be document-scraping-based, not API-based, except for ECB and MNB downloadable table sets.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations for pipeline engineering effort and refresh reliability for the highest-priority metric in HU payments.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Hungarian for a Banking Association-published, recurring quantitative banking-sector statistics series (analogous to the German or Austrian association datasets). No association-hosted statistical dataset page surfaced; sector aggregates in results came from the MNB (central bank) and from individual banks' annual reports, not from Magyar Bankszövetség.
negative_findings.result_summary: Association output appears to be qualitative (communiques, position papers, journal articles) rather than a standing statistics series; the quantitative banking-sector series in HU sits with the MNB, which belongs to another coverage cell.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents over-tasking cell 5 with a statistics-extraction pipeline that has no target; A4 quantitative banking aggregates must be sourced from the supervisor/central bank instead.

negative_findings.description: For the Magyar Fintech Szövetség (hunfintech.com) and EFISZ (efisz.hu) I did not reach a confirmed, enumerable member-directory URL within this pass; membership information came from secondary trade-media coverage (founding members for EFISZ, member categories for HFA).
negative_findings.result_summary: Association homepages identified and confidently attributed, but the specific member-list endpoints remain unverified hypotheses rather than found URLs.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The member lists are the highest-value pointer assets in this cell; a follow-up pass should navigate both sites directly to locate them.

negative_findings.description: Local-language searches for a Hungarian card-issuer or ATM-operator association (terms tried around bankkártya, ATM üzemeltető, kártyakibocsátó szövetség) returned no dedicated body; the functional equivalents are EFISZ on the payment-provider side and the Banking Association's internal working groups.
negative_findings.result_summary: No standalone HU cards/ATM association identified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Card and ATM statistics for HU will not come from an association layer; expect the central bank and international card schemes to be the only aggregators.

negative_findings.description: English-language searching for 'Hungarian Banking Association sector statistics publication' returned mainly Hungarian-language assets; only EFISZ was observed to maintain an explicit /en/ path. Most association output in this cell exists in Hungarian only.
negative_findings.result_summary: English is a shallow entry point for this cell; Hungarian-language collection is mandatory rather than optional.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any downstream collector configured English-first would miss the large majority of this cell's content.

negative_findings.description: The Factoring Association appears with two statistics paths in indexes: https://faktoringszovetseg.hu/statistikak-style path and a legacy http://www.faktoringszovetseg.hu/html/statisztika.html. I did not fetch either, so neither is claimed live.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two candidate URLs recorded; canonical one to be determined by the deterministic liveness pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids anchoring a recurring collector on a stale legacy path.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated Hungarian-language press room / 'sajtószoba' was located for Barion Payment Zrt. in this pass; searches on 'Barion sajtószoba blog statisztika' returned only product, customer-service and third-party integration pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Barion's public HU surface appears to be product/knowledge-base and price-list oriented rather than statistics-publishing; no recurring transaction-volume disclosure was found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The HU-owned #2 online PSP may not self-publish volumes, so its scale will have to be inferred from filed annual accounts and third-party estimates instead of press material.

negative_findings.description: For Cardnet Zrt. no corporate website was confirmed in this pass — only a LinkedIn company page surfaced in HU-language search results.
negative_findings.result_summary: Actor confirmed to exist and to operate in POS terminal servicing / cash registers / loyalty cards, but no primary web source established.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A material terminal-servicing actor would otherwise be missing from the source map; it needs a register-based rather than web-based tracking approach.

negative_findings.description: The Euronet HU press page (euronetatms.hu/sajtokozlemeny/) was fetched and returned content whose most recent datable items were 2016/2022; no 2024-2026 releases were observed on that page in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: HU ATM counts obtainable there (~420 independent ATMs, ~350 EUR-capable) are dated and must not be used as current figures.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Relying on this page alone would produce a stale view of the largest independent ATM estate in Hungary; parent-company SEC filings and bank outsourcing notices are needed for currency.

negative_findings.description: Euronet Worldwide's investor materials disclose installed ATM counts by segment/region (EFT Processing) but Hungary-level breakouts were not found in the results reviewed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Country-level ATM estate for HU is not a disclosed line item in parent filings.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets expectations: parent filings give direction and regional context only; HU-specific ATM counts require local press, bank notices or MNB data.

negative_findings.description: SimplePay (OTP Mobil) has no public price list; fees are set individually at contracting and only indicative offers circulate (an indicative offer PDF was seen hosted on a third-party merchant domain).
negative_findings.result_summary: Acquiring/PSP pricing for the market-leading HU PSP is not publicly published.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any HU online-acceptance pricing series will be structurally incomplete at the top of the market and must lean on Barion's public list plus scattered indicative offers.

negative_findings.description: All URLs recorded in this slice except https://www.euronetatms.hu/sajtokozlemeny/ were taken from search-result metadata and were not individually fetched in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: URLs are provided with confidence scores; liveness is to be established by the deterministic verification pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents a false impression of verification; corporate newsrooms (Visa, Mastercard) frequently reorganise URL paths, and the Mastercard HU newsroom already exhibits two distinct historical path patterns.

negative_findings.description: No HU systemic bank was found to publish a standing, machine-readable series of card counts, ATM fleet size or POS terminal counts. Where such figures appear, they are prose or chart values inside PDF annual reports and investor decks, and definitions differ per bank.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches in Hungarian for 'bankkártya darabszám', 'ATM hálózat', 'kártyaforgalom' returned report landing pages and PDFs, never a data table or API.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any cross-bank card/ATM/POS series must be hand-normalised from PDFs; the pipeline needs PDF table/OCR extraction plus a per-bank definition map, not a feed reader.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated 'digital bank KPI deck' was found for the unlisted HU banks (K&H, Erste HU, Raiffeisen HU, UniCredit HU, CIB). Only OTP, MBH and Gránit run genuine investor-presentation programmes; the other five publish statutory reports only.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches for 'befektetői prezentáció' plus each bank name surfaced statutory reports and parent-group material, not subsidiary KPI decks.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Digital-payment KPIs for over half the cell must be sourced indirectly from parent groups or media, lowering comparability and timeliness.

negative_findings.description: No stable Hungarian bank-side term was found for merchant-acquiring volume equivalent to 'POS acquiring volume'. Candidate phrasings ('elfogadói forgalom', 'kártyaelfogadás', 'POS terminál darabszám') were used but did not surface bank-published acquiring statistics in this cell's searches.
negative_findings.result_summary: Acquiring-side terminology appears to live with the regulator and with acquirer/PSP entities rather than in bank IR language.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Acquiring coverage for this cell is likely unreachable from bank IR alone and must be triangulated with regulator and PSP-side cells.

negative_findings.description: Two commercially useful aggregators are restricted: OPTEN company reports are paid, and portfolio.hu's deeper bank analysis sits behind Portfolio Premium. The e-beszamolo bulk dataset is likewise only available via a paid/requested data-supply route, not by scraping.
negative_findings.result_summary: Paywall and bulk-data-request models observed on opten.hu, portfolio.hu/premium and e-beszamolo 'beszámoló állomány értékesítése'.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Budget and licensing decisions are needed if systematic cross-bank financial normalisation is wanted; free routes cover primary documents only.

negative_findings.description: Parent-group IR portals (KBC, Erste Group, RBI, Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit Group) were inferred from ownership structure and included with root-level URLs only; they were not fetched in this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: URLs supplied as high-confidence-but-unverified starting points, not as confirmed live pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass should resolve these and locate the exact Hungary-segment report paths before they are relied upon.

negative_findings.description: Targeted Hungarian-language search for POS-terminal public procurement notices ('POS terminál közbeszerzés eredmény hirdetmény keretszerződés bankkártya') returned only commercial bank/acquirer marketing pages (OTP, Erste, MBH, SimplePay) and generic Public Procurement Authority pages — no specific POS-terminal tender.
negative_findings.result_summary: Generic web search is a poor channel for POS-terminal tenders; the term 'POS terminál' is dominated by acquiring-service marketing noise.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: POS terminal procurement in Hungary is largely private-sector (banks/acquirers) and therefore outside Kbt.; the public-procurement channel will yield POS mainly via state-owned buyers, transport ticketing and municipal cash-desk systems. Retrieval must be done inside EKR/Értesítő/TED with CPV filters, not via open web search.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian card-personalisation (kártyaszemélyesítés / kártyagyártás) procurement notice or dedicated buyer channel was located in this pass; searches surfaced only TED/CPV background material, not an actual HU notice.
negative_findings.result_summary: Card-personalisation tenders not confirmed in this run.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Card personalisation for Hungary is mostly commissioned by commercial banks and card processors (private, not Kbt.-bound), so public tenders may exist only for state-linked issuers (e.g. Magyar Posta, state health/ID cards, transport cards). The cell's card-personalisation coverage is therefore weak and needs a dedicated CPV-driven pass.

negative_findings.description: No URL in this slice was fetched and verified for liveness; all entries are search-derived with permalink patterns observed in results. EKR and TED portals are JavaScript-heavy and may return 403/challenge to naive fetchers.
negative_findings.result_summary: Liveness and crawlability are hypotheses, not verdicts.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream deterministic verification must distinguish bot-defence (403/timeout, likely live) from genuine relocation (404). Do not mark EKR/TED as dead on a single failed fetch.

negative_findings.description: Searches for cash-in-transit incumbents surfaced only one concrete award (Magyar Posta cash transport/processing won by MPT Security Magyar Posta Takarék Biztonsági és Logisztikai Zrt., stated value 80,000,000 HUF in a 2020-era Értesítő record); no systematic list of Hungarian CIT procurement was assembled.
negative_findings.result_summary: Cash-logistics vendor landscape only partially mapped from procurement notices.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cash-logistics incumbency (MPT Security, and international CIT operators) is a core intelligence target; a CPV-based sweep on security/cash-transport codes is still required.

negative_findings.description: No Temenos or Sopra Banking Software press release naming a Hungarian bank go-live was found; results returned only generic global core-banking marketing pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Vendor newsrooms searched in English returned no HU-specific core banking implementation announcement.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: HU core-banking supplier landscape appears dominated by domestic/regional integrators (Takarékinfo, T-Systems, Capsys, Laurel) rather than the big international core vendors — or those wins are simply unannounced. Either way the international-vendor newsroom route is low-yield for HU core banking.

negative_findings.description: No Printec Hungary bank reference or case-study page surfaced in Hungarian-language search, despite Printec being an ATM/self-service vendor active in CEE.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hungarian query combining Printec with bank/reference/POS terms returned no Printec HU content.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The commissioning organisation's own regional presence is not discoverable through generic HU search, implying HU-market vendor visibility generally requires direct site crawls rather than search-engine discovery — a systematic bias to correct for.

negative_findings.description: No OpenWay, Worldline or Nexi announcement naming a Hungarian bank customer was found in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Combined English query returned only ACI Worldwide HU material.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests the HU payments processing supplier set is narrower than the CEE norm, or that these vendors serve HU through unnamed regional contracts; warrants a dedicated per-vendor site pass rather than a combined query.

negative_findings.description: No Glory, Giesecke+Devrient or Brink's Hungary bank reference/case study was found; Hungarian cash-equipment search returned CIT operators (G4S, MPT Security, Criterion) instead of equipment vendors.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language cash equipment query surfaced service providers, not banknote-processing machine suppliers.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cash-handling HARDWARE supplier mapping for HU banks remains an open gap; the CIT-operator layer is visible but the equipment layer is not.

negative_findings.description: Canonical corporate domains for CARDNET Zrt., ANY Biztonsági Nyomda, T-Systems Magyarország, G4S HU and Mastercard's HU newsroom were inferred from company records and media pickups rather than confirmed by direct fetch in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Company-register and social/aggregator pages confirmed the entities; canonical URLs recorded at reduced confidence.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These URLs must be treated as unverified hypotheses; the deterministic liveness pass should resolve them, and a 403 should not be read as dead.

negative_findings.description: Hungary is not a CPMI member jurisdiction, so BIS Red Book statistics are not expected to carry a Hungarian country table or HU reference area.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches on BIS Red Book + Hungary returned only methodology and generic CPMI-country material; no HU country table surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents wasted collection effort against BIS for HU series; BIS should be scoped to peer benchmarking and definitions only.

negative_findings.description: ECB SPACE (payment attitudes / cash usage survey) covers euro area countries only; Hungary, being outside the euro area, is not a survey country.
negative_findings.result_summary: SPACE 2019/2022/2024 material consistently framed as 'euro area'; no Hungarian sample identified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Hungarian cash-usage behaviour must come from MNB's own household payment surveys or Findex, not SPACE; SPACE is a comparator only.

negative_findings.description: The 2025 EBA/ECB Report on Payment Fraud excludes Hungary because data were not available over the entire reporting period.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search result text explicitly states Hungary is excluded from the analysis for lack of full-period data.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: HU card-fraud benchmarking against EU peers is currently not possible from the supranational layer; must be sourced nationally from MNB.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian-language interface or publication was found for ECB Data Portal, BIS, IMF FAS or World Bank Findex; only Eurostat exposes a partial /hu Statistics Explained layer.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hungarian-language query returned Eurostat /hu explainer pages plus KSH and Hungarian media/academic secondary coverage, but no HU-language supranational statistical portal.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Hungarian-language discovery in this cell mostly finds secondary re-reporting of EU/IMF data (media, KSH, ASZ analyses) rather than the aggregators themselves; local-language search must be routed to national cells instead.

negative_findings.description: Eurostat does not publish card/ATM/POS payment transaction statistics; those belong to the ECB payment statistics domain. Eurostat's contribution for this cell is digital-economy and e-commerce demand-side indicators only.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hungarian-language Eurostat query surfaced ISOC datasets (isoc_ci_in_h, isoc_ec_ibuy, isoc_pibi_*) but no payments dataset.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids misassigning payment-statistics collection to Eurostat and clarifies the ECB/Eurostat division of labour.

coverage_gaps.description: Exact canonical URLs for the settlement-systems (VIBER/BKR/KELER) release, the Pénzforgalom 2030 PDF, and the archive index were inferred from parent pages rather than fetched individually.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a shallow crawl of statisztika.mnb.hu/publikacios-temak/penzforgalmi-adatok two levels deep to canonicalise all child URLs before scheduling collection.

coverage_gaps.description: The workbook layer (sheet names, indicator granularity, history depth, revision policy) of the quarterly payments release was not inspected.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Download one recent release workbook and one from ~3 years back; document sheet structure and any series breaks vs the 2001-2013 archive.

coverage_gaps.description: Denomination-level banknote/coin volume time series (as opposed to the aggregate value of currency in circulation) were not located as a downloadable dataset.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check the bankjegy-és-érme pages and the MNB balance-sheet release annexes for a denomination table; if absent, treat press releases and the Annual Report as the denomination source and log it as a structural limitation.

coverage_gaps.description: MNB supervisory statistics (felügyeleti statisztikák) and payment-oversight/enforcement publications were not explored, though they may carry institution-level payment and card acquiring detail.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout statisztika.mnb.hu/publikacios-temak/felugyeleti-statisztikak and MNB oversight/enforcement decisions in a follow-up cell.

coverage_gaps.description: It is unknown which fields the Intézménykereső exposes per entity (licence number, activity codes, licence date, status, address, ownership) and whether historic/withdrawn licences remain queryable.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run an interactive session against intezmenykereso.mnb.hu, inspect the network calls behind the search form, and document the field schema plus whether revoked entries persist.

coverage_gaps.description: Registers likely relevant to the payments actor map were not explored in this cell: virtual-asset/crypto service provider registration under MiCA, the MNB's cash-processing (készpénzfeldolgozó) authorisations, and the payment/securities settlement system oversight lists (GIRO, KELER, VIBER operators).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend searches with 'MNB kriptoeszköz-szolgáltató nyilvántartás MiCA', 'MNB készpénzfeldolgozási tevékenység engedély', 'MNB felvigyázás fizetési rendszer GIRO KELER VIBER'.

coverage_gaps.description: For several HU-language sources (Fizetési rendszer jelentés, FinTech report, Aranykönyv, decisions search) the exact English-edition URLs were not captured, only their existence inferred.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Map each HU page to its /en/ counterpart and record both URLs, so downstream collection can pick the language with the richer data tables.

coverage_gaps.description: An MNB archive tree (www.mnb.hu/archivum/...) holds legacy PSZAF-era supervisory statistics including older Aranykönyv editions, but its structure and coverage span were not mapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Crawl the /archivum/Felugyelet/ tree to establish how far back per-institution supervisory data reaches and where the break in methodology (PSZAF to MNB, 2013) sits.

coverage_gaps.description: Retail/commerce trade press (e.g. Trade magazin, Piac és Profit, Növekedés.hu) was not searched; these carry merchant-side acceptance, cash-handling and checkout-technology data that banking media omit.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run hu queries such as 'Trade magazin kártyaelfogadás kiskereskedelem adatok' and 'Piac és Profit önkiszolgáló kassza bankkártyás fizetés' in a follow-up pass.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language Hungary-focused business media (Budapest Business Journal / bbj.hu, Hungary Today, Daily News Hungary, Telex English) was not covered in this slice; searches skewed hu-language by design.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add an en-language pass targeting bbj.hu and similar for HU payments/banking market figures aimed at foreign investors, which often restate HU data with different framing.

briefs: The MNB source landscape for Hungarian payment, card, ATM/POS and cash statistics is bifurcated between two hosts: statisztika.mnb.hu carries the machine-oriented statistical releases (the quarterly 'Tájékoztató - Pénzforgalom' with cards/ATM/POS/accounts/fraud/revenues, the VIBER-BKR-KELER settlement release, the monthly balance-sheet release holding currency in circulation, plus calendar, methodology and glossary), while www.mnb.hu carries the analytical and narrative layer (Fizetési rendszer jelentés / Payment Systems Report, Pénzforgalom 2030, MNB-tanulmányok and MNB-szemle, the bankjegy-és-érme cash pages, the Annual Report and the year-indexed press releases). Both HU and EN editions exist for the flagship report and the payments release, but legacy mnb.hu/en/statistics deep links are stale (404 observed) and should be canonicalised to statisztika.mnb.hu. No MNB open API for these series was found, so file-level acquisition will need rendering-capable fetching of the release pages, with the ECB Data Portal PTT dataset as the structured, API-accessible mirror of the same MNB-reported figures. Highest-value tracking targets are the quarterly payments release, the annual Payment Systems Report, the monthly currency-in-circulation series, and the 2001-2013 archive for long-run back-series.

Hungary's supervisory/registry layer is unusually concentrated: the MNB is the single integrated authority, so one institution (mnb.hu plus the statisztika.mnb.hu and intezmenykereso.mnb.hu subdomains) holds the definitive index of every bank, e-money issuer, payment institution and PSD2 third-party provider operating in the country. The strongest pointer assets are the Intézménykereső search register, the open-banking ASPSP and AISP/PISP lists, and the Határozatok és végzések decision database, which together give both a current actor map and an entry/exit signal; the EBA PSD2 central register is the machine-readable mirror when automation matters. On the analytical side the Aranykönyv provides per-institution financials as a time series, while the Fizetési rendszer jelentés, the FinTech és Digitalizációs jelentés, Hitelintézeti Szemle and the MNB-tanulmányok series carry aggregate card, POS/ATM and cash-usage statistics with methodology. The main structural gap is that no register enumerates POS acquirers or ATM operators as such — that landscape must be derived from licence-activity fields cross-referenced with the payment reports.

Hungary's payments/banking trade-media layer is small, concentrated and unusually quantitative: Portfolio.hu's Bank desk, the VG group's bonline.hu, and the two fintech specialists (FinTechZone, Fintech.hu) between them convert almost every MNB pénzforgalmi release into charted analysis within days, and add acquirer- and vendor-level figures obtained by interview — qvik volumes from SimplePay, the first-ever decline in physical card-accepting locations, PSP revenue and fraud-loss totals. A second, structurally different tier consists of comparison portals (Bank360, Bankmonitor, Biztosdöntés, Money.hu) that compile bank-by-bank account, card and cash-withdrawal fee data from hirdetmény documents; this pricing data is genuinely unavailable in aggregated form anywhere else and is best treated as a direct source, subject to ToS checks. Consumer-facing volume outlets (Pénzcentrum, Origo, the county-daily network) are low-credibility on their own but give early and geographically granular signals on ATM-network restructuring and cash-access rule changes. Nothing in this cell publishes machine-readable data, so collection must be HU-language text extraction with mandatory reconciliation back to statisztika.mnb.hu; note also that 'POS terminál' is a heavily vendor-spammed query term and that neither napi.hu nor vg.hu produced any article-level hits in this pass.

Hungary's consultancy/academic layer on payments splits into three clusters: Big-4 and strategy firms (Deloitte HU with its Digital Banking Maturity local cuts, PwC HU's own 'Digitális Pénzügyi Körkép' consumer survey, KPMG HU financial services, McKinsey Budapest) publishing lead-generation thought leadership; commercial research houses (GKID/GKI Digital, NRC, eNET, plus the Mastercard-sponsored GKID 'Digitális Kereskedelmi Körkép') which own the only regular non-regulator series on online payment-method mix and cash-on-delivery share; and an academic tier centred on Corvinus, whose full texts sit in the open unipub and REAL repositories and whose payment-habits and cash-network work is often published through MNB paper series, Közgazdasági Szemle or the Banking Association's Gazdaság és Pénzügy. Discovery is best driven by pointer media (FinTechZone, Portfolio.hu, HWSW's deep eNET/GKI archive), since consultancy studies are announced through the press before or instead of being indexed anywhere. Main weaknesses of this cell: full research-house reports are commercial, EY Hungary shows no payments-specific output, and nothing found addresses ATM/POS acceptance-network economics — that topic needs its own targeted Hungarian-language sweep.

Hungary's cash-cycle intelligence splits cleanly into a regulator layer and a commercial layer. MNB is the anchor: it licenses cash processors (with a downloadable register), owns the banknote printer Pénzjegynyomda (which publishes audited accounts), sets cash-handling methodology, and publishes the ATM/cash time series in Pénzforgalmi adatok and the Fizetési rendszer jelentés. The 2025 ATM Act plus MNB decrees on minimum per-bank ATM counts create a compliance-reporting driver, though no public per-settlement ATM compliance register was found — deployment must be inferred from MNB statistics, government press, bank disclosures and independent deployer Euronet. The CIT/cash-processing market itself (G4S Készpénzlogisztikai, Criterion, Prompt Security, Risec, TrezEx and a long tail) is opaque by design, so the highest-yield collection routes are e-beszámoló filings, company registries, public procurement award notices, and occasional investigative reporting.

Hungary's legislative and fiscal channel for payments intelligence is highly centralised and well-digitised: Magyar Közlöny plus njt.hu carry every binding threshold (transaction levy rates under Act CXVI of 2012, the 2025 merchant cash-acceptance obligation, and the free-ATM-withdrawal limits raised to HUF 300k from February 2026), while parlament.hu bill reasonings expose the fiscal-yield and payment-volume assumptions behind each change. The tax side is strong on rules but weak on published data: NAV issues an annual guidance leaflet on the levy and maintains a public-data/FOI route, but no per-instrument levy revenue series was found, so the levy-as-payment-volume proxy must be rebuilt from budget aggregates plus statutory rates or requested under FOI. The consumer-protection side is the most quantitatively usable: MNB's annual Pénzügyi fogyasztóvédelmi jelentés and the Pénzügyi Békéltető Testület annual reports give consistent multi-year complaint and case counts broken down by product, an indirect read on card, ATM and account usage frictions. Main open gaps are the Ministry of Finance monthly budget release, the MNB supervisory decision register (IFR/payments enforcement), and GVH competition cases on card fees.

Hungary's payments weak-signal landscape is unusually concentrated: a handful of Hungarian-language hubs — Portfolio.hu's conference arm, FinTechZone (which also runs the FinTechShow/TechShow event brand), the Mastercard Év Bankja awards and the MNB's Fizetési Rendszer Fórum — carry most of the forward-looking disclosure, with named MNB, GIRO and bank executives repeatedly presenting transaction volumes and roadmap dates on stage well before official statistics appear. Infrastructure and operator sites (GIRO plus its career portal, Euronet's ATM newsroom, bank ATM-migration notices) and public procurement notices for card acceptance and POS services supply the hardest quantitative early signals, while job boards (Profession, Indeed, Jooble) reveal acquiring, POS and instant-payment build programmes through vacancy text. Funding and market-entry signals exist but only as scattered prose across trade and general media — there is no structured Hungarian funding dataset. The main uncovered channel is LinkedIn, which is where much of this community announces first and which cannot be collected compliantly at scale; the vendor/ISO layer of the POS and ATM market also still needs systematic enumeration.

For Hungary, the archival layer of payment/banking statistics is unusually well anchored: the MNB itself operates an explicit 'Archív tartalmak' section under Pénzforgalmi adatok that preserves 2001-2013 card-business, ATM/POS acceptance, chip-migration, interbank-turnover and card-fraud series that no longer appear in the live tables, and the ECB Data Portal keeps the discontinued PSS/Blue Book dataset with harmonised pre-2014 HU card and terminal series (API-only). Beyond these two anchors, recovery depends on web archives — the Internet Archive for mnb.hu and giro.hu (whose BKR turnover PDFs rotate off opaque storage URLs), since the Hungarian national web archive at OSZK is largely closed for copyright reasons. The Hungarian open-data layer is a cadastre/metadata-search stack (kozadatportal.hu, opendata.gov.hu, kozadat.hu) rather than a dataset store, so it functions as a pointer to holders rather than a download source, while KSH's STADAT archive, yearbooks and Statisztikai Szemle archive supply the historical and methodological trail. Priority actions are a file-level manifest of the six MNB archive sub-pages and a Wayback CDX sweep of the core HU payment domains.

Hungary's non-central-bank payments telemetry sits in two very different places: KSH, which publishes rich open retail-turnover and household-ICT series but exposes payment-method splits only inside narrative ICT/e-commerce publications rather than as maintained tables; and NAV, which holds by far the deeper asset — receipt-level online cash register and e-receipt data covering practically the whole retail till population, now extending through the e-pénztárgép/eNyugta regime — but publishes no aggregate payment-mode series and scopes machine access to each taxpayer's own registers. The practical collection strategy is therefore open scraping of KSH STADAT (bel* and ikt* families) plus PDF extraction from KSH ICT publications, combined with regulatory monitoring of NAV's eNyugta specification and Online Számla schema to know what fields the state actually captures. The highest-value unexplored move is a formal public-interest data request to NAV for anonymised aggregate cash-register turnover by payment mode, and retrieval of the cash-register/e-receipt decrees to confirm that payment mode is a mandatory reported field.

Hungary's payment-infrastructure operator layer is concentrated in three entities: GIRO Zrt. (BKR clearing plus the GIROInstant platform behind the AFR instant scheme and the qvik QR overlay), KELER Zrt. (CSD) and KELER KSZF/CCP — all overseen by the MNB, which is also their main statistical publisher. The operators themselves publish unevenly: GIRO has no statistics section and releases its 'BKR tranzakciók száma' series as hashed PDF assets whose current vintages could not be located in this pass, while KELER publishes daily/weekly/monthly/annual statistics including machine-readable daily CSVs. The most reliable structured series for BKR, VIBER and KELER turnover therefore sits on statisztika.mnb.hu (payment and securities settlement systems operation, plus the quarterly pénzforgalmi táblakészlet that also carries qvik adoption metrics), with the ECB Data Portal providing harmonised CCP/payment series for cross-country benchmarking. Practical collection for this cell should be document-scraping-first against giro.hu/dokumentumok and keler.hu, with MNB statistics as the authoritative fallback and MNB press releases plus Hungarian fintech trade press as the fast early-signal layer.

Hungary's association layer for banking and payments is concentrated in four bodies: Magyar Bankszövetség (the banking peak association, whose ~67-member 'Tagjaink' page is the master actor map including infrastructure members KELER and BISZ, and which publishes the quarterly journal Gazdaság és Pénzügy plus communiques rather than a statistics series), EFISZ (the Electronic Payment Service Providers Association, founded by GIRO, Magyar Posta, Magyar Telekom, OTP and others, and the only association running its own electronic-payment behaviour research), the Magyar Fintech Szövetség for the non-bank provider ecosystem, and OKSZ for the merchant/acceptance side, where roughly a third of Hungarian retail turnover sits and where the public fight over mandatory cash acceptance versus card acceptance is being argued. A second tier of associations does publish genuine member-aggregated numbers - the Leasing Association's quarterly placement volumes and the Factoring Association's turnover and GDP-penetration series are the cleanest quantitative assets in this cell - while MKIK and its research institute GVI supply long-running enterprise surveys with financial-sector breakouts. The important negative result is that no association publishes a recurring HU banking, card or ATM statistics series and no dedicated cards/ATM association exists, so A4's quantitative core must come from the central bank cell; associations here are best treated as pointer and positioning sources. Coverage is overwhelmingly Hungarian-language (only EFISZ was seen with an English track), so English-first collection would miss most of this landscape.

Hungary's commercial card/ATM/POS disclosure landscape is dominated by two card schemes with active HU press rooms — Mastercard (newsroom.mastercard.com/eu/hu, home of the 15-year 'Bankkártya Használati Szokások' survey and the Doppio acceptance-expansion programme) and Visa (visa.hu 'Visa szerkesztőség') — which publish HU-specific card penetration, contactless, mobile-wallet and acceptance-point figures earlier and more granularly than official statistics. On the acquiring/PSP side the richest operational numbers come from OTP Mobil/SimplePay via OTP Bank's news page (transaction counts, >23k partner merchants, average basket value), with Barion as the only actor publishing a transparent public price list; bank acquirers (OTP, K&H via khpos.hu, MBH, Erste via Global Payments) and independent terminal operators (Worldline/Bizpay, Nexi Central Europe, Fizetési Pont/OFSZ, Cardnet) disclose product detail but almost no volumes. ATM coverage is the weakest link: Euronet is the key independent deployer but its HU press page appears stale (counts dated 2016/2022), parent-company SEC filings give no Hungary breakout, and the most datable signals arrive indirectly through bank ATM-outsourcing notices and business-media reporting. Practical strategy: event-driven monitoring of scheme and operator press rooms as leading indicators, trade outlets (FinTechZone, Fintech.hu) as discovery feeds, and filed annual accounts from the Hungarian company register as the hard, legally-mandated proxy where operators publish no volumes.

Hungary's systemic bank issuers/acquirers split into two disclosure regimes: three genuine investor-communicating banks (OTP, MBH, Gránit) that publish quarterly reports and KPI-bearing investor decks, and five foreign-owned subsidiaries (K&H, Erste HU, Raiffeisen HU, UniCredit HU, CIB) that publish only statutory annual and Pillar 3 reports, with their Hungarian digital/card KPIs surfacing instead in parent-group segment reporting. Three pointer hubs make the cell tractable and should be the collection backbone: the BÉT/BSE kibinfo archive, the MNB tőkepiaci közzétételek portal, and the Ministry of Justice e-beszámoló register, each of which mirrors bank filings more durably than the banks' own CMS. The operational metrics this workstream wants — card counts, ATM fleet size, POS/acquiring volumes, mobile-wallet adoption — exist only as prose or chart values inside PDFs, with per-bank definitions, so the pipeline needs PDF/deck extraction and a normalisation map rather than any feed. Acquiring-side and cash-throughput figures were not found on the bank side at all and will have to come from the regulator and PSP cells.

Hungary's procurement channel for payments intelligence is unusually well-structured: EKR (ekr.gov.hu) carries the full procedure documentation for essentially every domestic tender, the Közbeszerzési Hatóság publishes the Közbeszerzési Értesítő and a CPV-searchable database of notices and contracts, and above-threshold contracts duplicate onto TED with a free, authentication-free Search API and monthly XML bulk packages — making a deterministic CPV-driven pipeline entirely feasible. The richest quantitative disclosures for our topics come from state-linked buyers: Magyar Posta (cash transport and cash processing, incumbent MPT Security), the MNB (banknote-processing systems with multi-year maintenance), and transport operators BKK and MÁV, whose ticket-vending-machine tenders quantify unattended card-acceptance fleets and even the cash-vs-card mix (card share above 70% of BKK automat purchases; dozens of card-only devices). Demand is currently being driven by statute: the 2025. évi XVIII. törvény and 19/2025 (VI.26.) MNB rendelet mandate ATM installation in every settlement of 1,000+ residents and force joint installation/operation contracts between payment service providers, so an ATM procurement wave should be visible in these channels. The main weaknesses of this cell are POS terminals and card personalisation, which in Hungary are mostly bought by private banks and processors outside the Public Procurement Act, and the absence so far of a systematic CPV sweep — both should be closed before treating procurement as a complete indicator of fleet size or vendor share.

Hungary's private-bank supplier ecosystem is legible mainly from the vendor side: international vendors (ACI Worldwide, Tietoevry, Diebold Nixdorf) publish named HU bank deployments with occasional unit counts, while the domestic layer (Capsys, T-Systems Magyarorszag, Laurel, Takarekinfo, 4iG, CARDNET) exposes bank relationships through Hungarian-language reference and news pages that search engines index poorly. The highest-value quantified anchors are not vendor marketing at all but regulator-forced disclosure — the GVH 2019 card-acceptance sectoral inquiry and MNB decree 19/2025, which allocates 1,039 mandated ATMs bank-by-bank (OTP 428, MBH 195, K&H 117, Erste 104) and thereby telegraphs the 2025-2026 ATM procurement pipeline. Cash-cycle suppliers are visible as CIT operators (G4S, MPT Security, Criterion) but the banknote-equipment vendor layer and the POS hardware vendor layer remain unmapped. Recommended next step is direct sitemap-level crawling of vendor case-study libraries plus profiling of GIRO/BISZ, since search-engine discovery systematically under-represents this cell.

For Hungary, the supranational layer is dominated by the ECB Data Portal, which carries the harmonised MNB-reported card, ATM and POS terminal series (PSD/PAY/PTN/PTT dataflows) with a clean SDMX API and is the single highest-value target in this cell. The IMF Financial Access Survey and World Bank Findex/WDI add long annual ATM-density panels and the only cross-country comparable demand-side survey evidence for Hungarian card and digital-payment behaviour, while the EBA registers map the HU payment-institution actor landscape. Two structural exclusions matter: Hungary is outside CPMI (so BIS Red Book carries no HU country table) and outside the euro area (so ECB SPACE cash-usage data exclude HU), and the 2025 EBA/ECB payment fraud report drops Hungary for incomplete data. Eurostat contributes only demand-side digital-economy indicators, not payment statistics, and is the sole aggregator in this cell with any Hungarian-language surface.
